metric.capability_coverage.basis: capability_coverage over full fixed 88-point denominator per spec 6.1.5 / capability_universe.json
metric.capability_coverage.formula: C = 100 * (sum over 44 probes of capability_points * support_factor) / 88
metric.capability_coverage.instrument_note: This is a single-worker, single-language (Python) assessment produced against the frozen capability_universe.json probe set and support_rubric; it does not itself constitute V1-V5 pre-measurement validation across all ten languages, which is a cross-language obligation outside this work unit's scope.
metric.capability_coverage.na_policy_compliance: No probe was excluded or reweighted for Python. All NONE results (F04.P1, F04.P2, F05.P2, F08.P1, F20.P2) contribute 0 to the numerator and their full 2 capability points to the fixed 88-point denominator per NA-2, and each carries a written justification citing the applicable language-documentation fact per NA-6/NA-5. Named-substitution PARTIALs (F02.P2, F12.P1, F12.P2, F14.P1, F15.P1, F15.P2) follow R9 and are recorded PARTIAL, never FULL, per the deterministic_tie_break.named_substitution rule.

F01.P1.reason: Python has no documented form for a binding guaranteed never-reassignable; ordinary assignment is used by convention only.

F01.P2.reason: No language-enforced immutable constant; module-level UPPER_CASE name is convention, not enforced by the language.

F02.P1.reason: Python requires no separate declaration step; v is definitely assigned on both branches and readable after, satisfying all numbered sub-requirements under the frozen recipe.

F02.P2.reason: Named substitution per R9: Python has no way to obtain genuinely uninitialized storage (bytearray/bytes are always zero/default-initialized); substituted default-initialized buffer written per canonical_task instruction, PARTIAL and never FULL.

F03.P1.reason: x += 1 is Python's normal in-place compound-assignment form for a mutable local int name; behavior fully delivered.

F03.P2.reason: xs[1] = 42 mutates the list in place through the existing name.

F04.P1.reason: Python scalar names bind immutable int objects; there is no documented mechanism for a second name to write the same scalar storage as an existing local (no references/pointers/inout for locals).

F04.P2.reason: Python list slicing always copies; there is no standard non-copying read-only view over a list's existing elements (memoryview applies only to buffer-protocol types, not list).

F04.P3.reason: `is` operator is Python's standard object-identity test; routing through a one-element list and reading back preserves identity.

F05.P1.reason: f(x) is Python's ordinary bare call form; objects are passed by object reference per Python's evaluation model.

F05.P2.reason: Python provides no documented mechanism for a callee to write a caller's scalar local variable; only mutable-container substitution is possible, which R9/probe text excludes as an acceptable FULL/PARTIAL substitute for this probe (mandated NONE per rubric N-4 listing).

F05.P3.reason: def/lambda closures capture enclosing locals; map(neg, xs) applies a by-name function value.

F06.P1.reason: Ordinary function returning xs[1], bound at call site with y = mid(xs); return y is standard.

F06.P2.reason: Python tuple return (a // b, a % b) with q, r = divmod2(a, b) is the standard multiple-result mechanism.

F07.P1.reason: r = a * b + c uses ordinary operators and precedence; Python ints are unbounded so no overflow trap changes the operator's expressibility.

F07.P2.reason: //, %, and / are Python's standard floor-division, remainder, and true-division operators.

F08.P1.reason: Python has no fixed-width 32-bit integer type or standard checked/wrapping/saturating 32-bit arithmetic operation; ints are arbitrary precision, so the overflow construct cannot be expressed with standard operators.

F08.P2.reason: Explicit guard 'q = 0 if b == 0 else a // b' is a standard local guard (rung ii), making the zero-divisor outcome determinate at the site.

F09.P1.reason: s1 == s2 compares string contents in Python, the ordinary equality operator.

F09.P2.reason: xs.sort(reverse=True) or sorted(xs, reverse=True) supplies an explicit descending order; a < b is the ordinary comparison operator.

F10.P1.reason: Python has no native 32-bit integer type; ctypes.c_int32(big).value (standard library) is required to obtain truncating/wrapping narrowing, a weaker/atypical substitute for a native narrowing conversion operator.

F10.P2.reason: i + d triggers Python's implicit int-to-float promotion in ordinary mixed arithmetic.

F11.P1.reason: xs[i] is the ordinary indexed-read form; raises IndexError deterministically on out-of-range, a documented, determinate outcome.

F11.P2.reason: xs[1:4] is Python's standard slice/sub-range form (list slicing).

F12.P1.reason: Named substitution per R9: Python has no enforced type-level optional distinction; None is used as an untyped absence sentinel, with 'x if x is not None else 0' or similar as the fallback form.

F12.P2.reason: Named substitution per R9: Python has no standard optional-aware chaining/mapping operator; an explicit conditional expression is substituted.

F13.P1.reason: int(s) raises ValueError on malformed input and propagates unhandled by Python's default exception-propagation semantics; no special declaration syntax is required or omitted.

F13.P2.reason: try/except around int(s) with a fallback value in the except clause is Python's standard local-handling construct.

F14.P1.reason: Python has no closed-sum-type declaration; a class hierarchy or dataclass union is the nearest standard substitute, but nothing in the language prevents a third case being added elsewhere, per R9 named substitution.

F14.P2.reason: Python's structural pattern matching (match/case) dispatches over Circle/Rect without a default arm and computes area; exhaustiveness enforcement is an observation-target item, not a support requirement.

F14.P3.reason: Python's duck typing/ABC mechanism trivially allows a Tri class defined in a separate module to implement area() and be dispatched through the abstract interface without editing the shapes unit.

F15.P1.reason: Per the canonical_task's own named substitution clause: Python has only a universal dynamic type, no enforced parametric generics; the nearest standard (untyped) function form is substituted.

F15.P2.reason: Per the canonical_task's own named substitution clause: Python has no declaration-site constraint mechanism enforced by the language; ordinary comparison operators are used without an enforced bound.

F15.P3.reason: Python's dynamic typing/duck typing trivially holds heterogeneous concrete types A and B in one list under an informal Named 'interface' and dispatches tag() at runtime.

F16.P1.reason: xs = [1, 2, 3]; total = sum(xs) is Python's standard literal and sum() builtin.

F16.P2.reason: dict literal, sum(mp.values()), and mp.get('b', 0) are Python's standard map construction, iteration, and lookup-with-default forms.

F17.P1.reason: with open('data.txt') as f: is Python's standard scoped-cleanup (context manager) mechanism guaranteeing release on every exit path including exceptions.

F17.P2.reason: Python's __del__ finalizer timing is documented as implementation-defined (not guaranteed deterministic across implementations); the nearest standard deterministic construct is an explicit close()/dispose invoked by a `with`-scoped wrapper, which is the substituted PARTIAL form.

F18.P1.reason: print('x') requires no import in Python (builtin), satisfying the canonical_task's 'nothing if the facility is available without one' branch.

F18.P2.reason: Python module privacy (leading underscore on secret()) is a documented convention, not an enforced boundary; the language does not prevent external access, so the nearest standard convention is substituted.

F19.P1.reason: asyncio (standard library) with asyncio.gather over two coroutines and asyncio.run() as the entry point is Python's standard async facility.

F19.P2.reason: Two asyncio tasks incrementing a shared counter with no await inside the increment loop are documented by asyncio's cooperative single-threaded scheduling guarantee (a task runs uninterrupted until it awaits), giving a documented race-free discipline without needing an explicit lock; a threading.Lock-based alternative is equally standard.

F20.P1.reason: ctypes.CDLL (standard library, shipped with CPython) declares and calls libc abs(-3), Python's built-in FFI mechanism with no third-party package.

F20.P2.reason: N-1/instrument note per rubric: `python3 FILE.py` produces no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe, so the nm-based unmangled-symbol verification cannot apply; recorded as NONE with nm evidence field 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe', not as N/A (per na_policy NA-5/6 and the F20.P2 canonical_task note).
